prompt: A geometric sequence starts at $a_1 = 3$ and multiplies by $r = 2$ each step. Find $a_8$.
hint: Use $a_n = a_1 \times r^{\,n-1}$. Again the exponent is one LESS than the term number.

hints.text: Use $a_n = a_1 \times r^{\,n-1}$. Again the exponent is one LESS than the term number.

alternativeExplanations.title: Just keep doubling
steps: Count them: that is eight terms, so the last one is a₈.
384 — doubling by hand is quick when n is small, and it double-checks the formula.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the multiplications
steps: Term 1 has been multiplied zero times. Term 2 once. Term 3 twice.
So term 8 has been multiplied 7 times — that is where the exponent 7 comes from.
